quote: Serotonin is now removed only by saturable enzymes, which is why the effect takes about a month to reach a baseline level.
source: transcript 9/29 (~20%) does say 'it’s gonna take about a month before you reach some sort of a baseline level', but the question asks only which curve is 5HT + fluoxetine; the month-to-effect sentence explains something not asked.
fix: Fluoxetine blocks SERT, the serotonin reuptake transporter, so more serotonin stays in the synapse. Serotonin appears more potent and its curve shifts to the left. Efficacy does not change: it is still serotonin, there is simply more of it.

quote: For the headache study that is about 325 mg, the regular-strength tablet, so dosing can start there; those who need 700 mg get Extra Strength (500 mg) or two tablets. Above 4000 mg/day is liver toxicity.
source: Part 2 pages 36–38 and transcript 9/29 carry these numbers, but the question asks what the 50% crossing is called; the tablet strengths and the 4000 mg/day limit are doses he said he will not test ('not slide 200 at the bottom in the smallest font').
fix: From the cumulative quantal data come the minimum dose that does something, the maximum dose, and the dose that takes care of half of the population, the effective dose 50 (ED50). For the headache study that is about 325 mg, 'the dose that takes care of 50% of you'.

source: transcript 9/29 (~92%): 'We’re going to have the effective dose, which is 10, that treats 99% of the patients, divided by the lethal dose, which is even smaller than that. ... My safe index is 1.1.' Spoken that way the ratio is 10/1 = 10; the slide (Part 2 page 42) gives SI = 1/10 = 0.1 and the item already notes the conflict. A student who follows his spoken words picks this distractor.
fix: keep the key (slide); strengthen the distractor why: '10/1 is the effective dose on top, which is how he read it aloud; the slide formula is SI = LD1/ED99 = 1/10 = 0.1, and either way the conclusion is the same: not a safe drug.'
